title: CHAPTER TWENTY-SIX. On things created in the beginning; heaven and earth
english: CHAPTER TWENTY-SIX. On those things which were created in the beginning, and namely on the highest heaven, Angels, and earth.

In the beginning God created heaven and earth — Genesis 1:1. Heaven here is taken both properly for the expanse and heavenly things, and figuratively. Figuratively either by metonymy or by synecdoche.

By metonymy: (1) For God its possessor and author — Daniel 4:26; Matthew 21; Luke 15:18,21; John 3:27. (2) For other heaven-dwellers — Job 15:15; Psalm 89:6. (3) For the church militant on earth — Daniel 8:10; Revelation 9:1; 12:7. (4) For meteors — Leviticus 26:19. By synecdoche: (1) For the highest heaven only — Mark 16:19. (2) For the starry heaven — Psalm 19:7. (3) For the air — Genesis 1:26. But in the present heaven is taken by Moses both for the angelic heaven and for the heaven-dwellers produced by God in the beginning: but Earth for the other principle, from which these interior things which the highest heaven encloses — except the rational soul or our immortal spirit — were produced later.

title: III: heaven produced in the beginning of time; angels
english: III. The heavens were produced in the beginning of time, and with them the Angels, intelligent spirits, created by God immediately.

Angels are spiritual substances, complete, incorporeal, understanding, willing, powerful. They are not eternal but created; they are not everywhere by essence as God is, but where God has willed them to be.
Orders and hierarchies are distinguished, concerning which one must judge soberly from Scripture, not from Pseudo-Dionysius.

title: Earth as incomplete principle; chaos; Cap. 26 toward Hexaemeron
english: Earth in the beginning was produced incompletely, as is clear from chapter 24. It was without form and void, and darkness was upon the face of the deep — Genesis 1:2.

That chaos was not eternal matter, but a created subject from which God on the following days brought forth distinct species. The Spirit of God was brooding upon the waters — Genesis 1:2 — preparing the matter for the Hexaemeron.
CHAPTER TWENTY-SEVEN, On the Hexaemeron or the works of the six days, follows.
